data: Run the console on a server

• Backups, PgBouncer, Tailscale and the TLS mode are set only at node creation.
  • up does not change resources that exist. For example, it does not add a node or change a server type.
  • Restore is not automated.
  • Replication is asynchronous. A failover can lose the last transactions that the replicas did not receive.
  • The load balancer hides the client address from Postgres.
  • Alerts are off unless you pass --monitor or run pgha monitor install. up does not install the timer on nodes that already exist.
  • Cloud-init user data must stay at or under 32 KiB. Backups, PgBouncer, Tailscale, and the monitor together still fit.
  • No automatic upgrades of PostgreSQL major versions.
  • Remote state stores the secrets as plain JSON in the remote database. pgha does not encrypt them a second time.
  • Console sessions end at a restart. A user removed from --auth-allow or from the provider keeps a running session until --session-ttl ends or the console restarts.
  • adopt works only with Hetzner Cloud servers and the Debian layout.
  • The object storage price in the bill comes from flags, not from the API.
  • Console monitoring keeps one hour in memory, only while someone views it. It is not a long-term metrics store. A console restart clears it.
  • The console edits rows only in tables with a primary key. The SQL editor shows the last statement's result, up to 1000 rows. Requests are limited to 1 MB.
